title: Job 20
paragraphs: ¹ Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said, ² My troubled thoughts urge me to reply — I am stirred within me. ³ I have heard a rebuke that dishonors me, and my understanding compels me to answer. ⁴ Surely you know how it has been from ancient times, since humans were first placed upon the earth — ⁵ that the triumph of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the godless lasts only a moment.

⁶ Though his greatness rises to the heavens and his head touches the clouds, ⁷ he will perish forever like his own dung. Those who once saw him will ask, 'Where has he gone?' ⁸ He will fly away like a dream and not be found; he will be chased off like a vision of the night. ⁹ The eye that saw him will see him no more; his own place will never look upon him again. ¹⁰ His children will beg from the poor; his own hands will give back his wealth.

¹¹ His bones are full of the sins of his youth, which will lie down with him in the dust. ¹² Though evil is sweet in his mouth, though he hides it under his tongue, ¹³ though he savors it and will not let it go, keeping it on his palate — ¹⁴ yet his food will turn sour in his stomach; it will become viper's venom inside him. ¹⁵ He has swallowed down riches and will vomit them up again; God will flush them out of his stomach.

¹⁶ He will suck the poison of serpents; the viper's tongue will kill him. ¹⁷ He will never see the rivers, the streams flowing with honey and cream. ¹⁸ He will give back what he worked for without enjoying it; he will gain no profit from his trade. ¹⁹ For he has oppressed the poor and left them with nothing; he has seized houses he did not build. ²⁰ He knew no rest in his greed; nothing he treasured could save him.

²¹ Nothing will be left for him to eat; his prosperity will not last. ²² In the midst of his plenty he will be in want — the full force of misery will come upon him. ²³ Just as he is filling his belly, God will unleash his burning anger upon him, raining it down on him in full force. ²⁴ He may flee from an iron weapon, but a bronze arrow will pierce him through. ²⁵ He pulls it out of his back, the gleaming point out of his liver — terrors overwhelm him.

²⁶ Total darkness is stored up for him; a fire that needs no fanning will consume him; what remains in his tent will be destroyed. ²⁷ The heavens will expose his guilt; the earth will rise up against him. ²⁸ The flood will sweep his house away; it will be carried off in the day of God's anger. ²⁹ Such is the fate God has laid up for the wicked — the inheritance appointed for them by God.
